title.narrative: Appui à la protection, l'accès aux services et à la résilience climatique aux réfugiés, personnes déplacées internes et communautés d'accueil des régions de Gao, Ménaka et Ségou

description.narrative: During 2024, Mali faced several challenges, including the continuation of armed conflicts, natural disasters and the energy crisis. This situation regularly destabilizes the protection environment and the survival framework of civilian populations faced with the threat of arbitrary detention, which causes psychosocial stress and is a trigger for population movements. This situation is corroborated by figures from the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) and UNHCR statistics from September 2024, which highlight an increase in the number of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) to 378,363 people. In addition, the 122,992 refugees from the sub-region were registered in Mali. In addition, there is the situation of victims of natural disasters, which is estimated at more than 380,000 people nationwide. These factors have contributed to exacerbating the severity of the needs, requiring a package of humanitarian assistance to more than 137,500 people in the heavily impacted regions.It is with this in mind that the project will be intended to meet the humanitarian needs of refugees, internally displaced persons and host communities heavily affected by this crisis in the regions of Ségou and Gao. It has provided a multi-sectoral response targeting 29,125 people with an integrated four-pronged approach including: 1) Shelter support and rehabilitation of damaged houses, and provision of non-food items; 2) Raising awareness of Housing, Land and Property (LTP) rights; 3) Support for victims of explosive devices; 4) Strengthening climate resilience. In terms of the first component, the planned response package, consists of providing transitional shelter assistance to the displaced and homeless, the rehabilitation and reinforcement of damaged houses for access to safe housing for 7,500 victims in the regions of Gao and Ségou, thus reducing the occupancy of classrooms. In addition, the necessary support in non-food items contributes to ensuring a functional domestic space for 3,125 people affected by the disaster in the Ségou region by reconstituting their essential household items. The second component will ensure the realization of awareness-raising sessions on the rights to housing, land and property (LTP) in situations of displacement in the regions of Ségou, Gao and Ménaka in order to strengthen the protection of the 1,300 most vulnerable households (6,500 people). Households in need of property documents will benefit from legal support from the competent authorities in this area. The third component will provide emergency assistance to victims of improvised explosive devices and equip 12,000 people most at risk through communication on the dangers and risks associated with IEDs and awareness raising to overcome the effects of the explosive threat in the regions of Gao and Ségou. Finally, the fourth component aims to support and strengthen climate resilience through the implementation of climate-resilient shelters to help 1,250 people heavily affected by floods to rebuild more safely, by optimizing their shelters to cope with future shocks.
